source_text: Quamvis nimis molliter egerim; etsi enim Christus ex eo quo venit tempore universis hominibus doceretur et iter interclusisse mortis et vitam donasse perpetuam, ut nemo prorsus ex eo die, quo Verbum caro factum est [n187] , aut in peccatum laberetur aut pro peccato poenam timeret, non tamen ea condicio primae iniquitatis, quae liberalitatis doceretur extremae, quoniam subvenire non merentibus potest et solet Deus cum laude clementiae, punire autem non peccantes non potest sine eversione iustitiae.
pass_a_gloss: Although I have acted too softly; for even if Christ from that time in which he came were taught both to have shut off the road of death for all human beings and to have given perpetual life, so that no one at all from that day on which the Word was made flesh either would slip into sin or would fear a punishment for sin, nevertheless that would not be the condition of the first iniquity which would be taught of the last liberality, since God can and is accustomed to come to help those not deserving with praise of clemency, but he cannot punish those not sinning without an overthrow of justice.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS mors; Blaise temporal vs eternal death in Rom 5

pass_b_english: Yet I have argued far too gently. Even if Christ were shown, from the time he came, to have blocked the road to death for all human beings and given everyone everlasting life—so that from the very day ‘the Word became flesh’ (John 1:14) absolutely no one fell into sin or feared punishment for sin—the first wickedness would still not have the same character as this later generosity. For God can and commonly does help the undeserving, earning praise for mercy; but he cannot punish those who have not sinned without overthrowing justice.

choices.why: Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.
Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)
